CBU.name: Consolidation Breakout Up
rule: Price bases in a tight range or holds a level, then one candle breaks UP out of it.
Entry: after that breakout candle closes (the ideal fill is the next candle's open).
Source: his own description of CBU while reviewing OFAL (2026-08-12). The setup list in his ENGU rulebook files CBU / CBD as 'consolidation breakout up / down', separate from ENGU.
findings: Futures, 12 trades: 7 winners, +$53.49, average +0.18 R. Stocks, 12 trades: 5 winners, -$133.56 (IPST alone -$164), average -0.45 R.

Signal-bar features: 7 of the 9 CBU signals that had an earlier regular-session candle closed at a new high of the day, 9 of 12 above the premarket high and 10 of 11 above the prior-day high, usually far above them: CBU is a new high on a day that is already strong. ENGU is the opposite.

6 of the 12 futures trades were bought inside the breakout minute itself, off a 5- or 10-second chart. The 1-minute candle closed after those fills, so they are left out of the chase and volume splits below (the page marks them "same bar").
Futures CBU at the open paid: 6 trades taken 09:30-10:00 averaged +0.33 R, the 6 taken later +0.03 R.

Volume: of the 6 futures trades whose breakout minute closed before the fill, the 4 whose 1-minute breakout candle traded 3x or more the volume of the 10 candles before it all won (+0.37 R average); the other 2 averaged -0.29 R. Counting all 12 it is +0.36 R against 0.00 R. Small numbers.

Exits leave money, but holding is not free: in the 15 minutes after the exit, price reached a median 1.4x the risk past his entry, yet it also came back through the breakout candle’s low on 6 of the 12 futures trades.

Stocks: every breakout candle is now read at 1 minute or finer (6 from the bars, 6 off his own charts). 10 of 12 fills sat no more than 10% of the candle’s range past its close (8 at or below it); only OFAL (+44%) and HOWL (+32%) chased. The earlier "chasing is the leak" reading came from 5-minute bars and does not hold.
Stock losses: three of the seven losers (SUGP, XRX and IPST, $178 of the $235 lost) went out at or through the breakout candle’s low. IPST was held 0.59 below it after the 11:05 candle broke it.
EHGO’s real breakout candle is 09:29 (low 2.88, the 2.87 stop he drew), not 09:31: that makes it a +0.53 R trade, not the +3.3 R the SCORE in TRADING LOG shows.

ENGU.name: Engulfing Up
rule: Context: a pullback holding a level (prior-day high/low, day high/low, premarket range, a demand zone) with room to the next level up.
Trigger: one large-body, small-wick candle that engulfs the candle(s) before it, on a clear volume spike versus its neighbours.
Entry: the open of the next candle. Stop: below the trigger candle's low. Target: the next level.
Source: his ENGU rulebook, written from his 1-minute ENGU trades (2026-07-04).
findings: Futures, 17 trades: 12 winners, +$107.25, average +0.10 R. Stocks, 1 trade: LABT, +$3.60, +0.19 R.

Signal-bar features: only 2 of 16 ENGU signals closed at a new high of the day, 2 of 17 above the premarket high, 2 of 17 above the prior-day high and 5 of 17 above the high of the 10 candles before: ENGU fires inside the day’s range, unlike CBU.
The open is where ENGU works: 8 trades taken 09:30-10:00 averaged +0.28 R (7 winners); the 9 taken later averaged -0.06 R (5 winners).

7 of the 17 futures trades were bought inside the 1-minute trigger candle itself (off a 5- or 10-second chart, or in the last second of the minute on 2026-09-22), so their chase cannot be measured from 1-minute bars. On the 10 that can, chase made no difference: 6 filled no more than 10% of the range past the close averaged +0.13 R, 4 filled further past it +0.12 R. The earlier "chase is the difference" reading leaned on those 7 in-candle fills.

Only 4 of the 17 trigger candles (16 one-minute, one 5-minute) traded 3x the volume of the 10 before them, although his rulebook calls the volume spike the number-one filter. On these trades the spike did not separate winners: 3 spike trades that closed before the fill averaged +0.07 R, the 7 without +0.15 R.

After the exit, price reached a median 1.1x the risk past his entry within 15 minutes. The best trade, 2026-09-22 MNQ (+0.53 R), is the one his note says he should have held: price ran 112 points past the entry within 15 minutes, about 2.2x the risk.
2026-09-08 was traded off the 5-minute chart and is measured on that 5-minute 13:00 candle: filled 7.5% of its range below the close, then timed out at -0.14 R.
